name: lumion
label: Lumion / Twinmotion / D5 (flattened)

maps.notes: sRGB. 2048 maximum, 1024 if the scene is heavy -- these engines are realtime and the texture budget is the whole cost.
8-bit on purpose: these engines compress it anyway, and the extra 8 bits buy nothing at walkthrough speed.
Clamped harder than the other presets: a flattened realtime material with a mirror patch or a pure-flat patch is the artefact a client notices.
8-bit, used as a bump only. The loaders in this class read a small amplitude and a 2048 map; a 16-bit 4k height file is discarded or downscaled on import anyway.

notes: Flatten everything: these engines want albedo, normal and roughness and not much else. No packed maps, no 16-bit, no AO map -- the occlusion in these renderers is their own.
Height is a bump, not displacement: keep the amplitude small and check it in motion, not in a still.
2048 maximum. If the scene is heavy, 1024, and put the detail in the geometry instead.

This preset writes the 8-bit height map the doc's matrix calls out as banding-prone. The recipe asks for it (these engines want small files), pack warns about it, and the warning is the point: it is a decision, not an oversight.
